newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Tighter BoE policy to boost cable soon.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Tighter BoE policy to boost cable soon.

text.p: Do not be fooled by sterling's recent stumble in its sprint to four-year highs -- tighter UK monetary policy will bolster the British currency above current levels for most of 1997, according to the Reuters quarterly U.S. economic poll.

The average forecast of 16 analysts surveyed last week showed sterling will rise to $1.6427 by the end of the first quarter and hold steady at around $1.6344 until the end of the year. In late U.S. trade Tuesday, it traded at $1.6185, well off its four-year high of $1.711 seen in early January.
A robust UK economy and looming monetary tightness suggest a rebound in the pound, said Sal Guatieri, senior economist at the Bank of Montreal in Toronto.

"We're expecting 100 points of tightening from the Bank of England through the course of this year," he said, adding that the Federal Reserve will likely keep U.S. official interest rates on hold for the year.
"We are expecting one move before the (May) elections in the UK and three moves for the rest of the year," he added.
A general election in Britain must be held by May 22 of this year and Britain's cabinet decided on Monday that it would aim to hold the election on May 1.
The pound will also benefit from expected weakness in the German mark as the build-up toward European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) grows, analysts said.
"We expect to see continued deutschemark weakness at least into early 1998," said Bruce English, a vice president at ABN-AMRO Bank.
"(Investors) want to be in Europe, but they want to stay outside of EMU because of possible bumpiness as you move into the period of setting rates -- the U.K. will tend to benefit a bit," he said.
The poll yielded a relatively narrow range of forecasts, with analysts seeing the pound as high as $1.76 and as low as $1.50 through the end of 1997.
